questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers be kept?

options.text: In a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be kept in a pouch on the driver's side door or in another spot the driver can reach easily while wearing a seat belt. The papers must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: A person watching a tank being loaded or unloaded must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials involved.

questions.explanation: The supervisor of a tank loading or unloading must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed. A chemical suit is not required.

questions.question: What information is on a hazardous materials shipping paper?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: A shipping paper describes the hazardous materials being transported. This includes shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests.

questions.question: When transporting mass explosives, what must you do?

options.text: The vehicle must always be placarded.
The vehicle only needs to be placarded if carrying more than 200 pounds.
The vehicle does not need to be placarded.
Only rural roads should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must always be placarded.
questions.explanation: Some hazardous materials only need placards when carrying 1,001 pounds or more. However, mass explosives must always have placards, even in small amounts.

questions.question: How should a shipper tell a driver about cargo risks?

options.text: By writing a note on a blank piece of paper
By putting hazard warning labels on packages
By placing orange dots on packages

questions.correctAnswerText: By putting hazard warning labels on packages
questions.explanation: Shippers must alert drivers and others to hazards using shipping papers, hazard warning labels on packages, emergency response information, and placards.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep copies of hazardous materials shipping papers?
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy of shipping papers for at least two years from when the initial carrier accepts the material. For hazardous waste, the time is three years.

questions.question: Who conducts the background check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass a background check by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: If a driver gets a leaking hazardous materials package, what should they do?

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road.
Get someone else to drive it.

questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse to transport packages or shipments of hazardous materials that are leaking.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, how far from buildings must you park?
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, place where people gather, or open fire.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials warning signs on vehicles?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the right placard?

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.
The type of container holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: You must know the hazard class of the materials being shipped. You also need to know the amount and total weight of all hazardous materials in your vehicle.

questions.question: When must you use a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard?

options.text: When shipping more than 50 pounds of the product.
When shipping more than 10 pounds of the product.
For any amount of the product.
When the product is in a non-sealed container.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any amount of the product.
questions.explanation: You must always display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard and the correct hazard class placard, even for small amounts of these materials.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
Attach a QR code that can be scanned.
Reduce the size of the label to fit it on the package.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a hazard warning label will not fit on the package, put the label on a tag and attach the tag securely to the package.

questions.question: What is required of a person supervising tank loading?

options.text: Not know the materials being loaded.
Stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch the tank loading. This person must stay alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, what comes first?

options.text: The materials written in larger text.
The materials written in red ink.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must be listed first on the shipping paper.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Always feel the doors to see if they are hot before opening them. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. If the doors are hot, leave them closed.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, what are they certifying?

options.text: The package does not contain hazardous materials.
The package was prepared following all the rules.
The package was packed at a specific location.
The package will be loaded on the trailer first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The package was prepared following all the rules.
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that the package was prepared according to all applicable rules.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo is leaking, what should the driver do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone to alert emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel.
questions.explanation: Stop driving as soon as it is safe. Park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with the vehicle, and send someone to get help. Continuing to drive will spread the contamination.

questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a package, which placard must be used?
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a package or shipping paper, you must display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard as appropriate.

questions.question: What must emergency response information from the shipper include?

options.text: The date the materials were packed.

questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include: basic descriptions and technical names of the materials; health hazards; fire or explosion risks; steps to take in case of accident; how to handle fires; how to handle spills or leaks; and first aid measures.

questions.question: What should a driver do if given a leaking package or shipment?

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse any leaking packages or shipments of hazardous materials.

questions.question: What is used to warn people about hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped warning signs called placards are placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials to warn others.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, what should be done?

options.text: Let it air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Areas exposed to corrosive liquids must be thoroughly washed with water.

questions.question: Where can a person attending a placarded vehicle be located?

options.text: Either awake or asleep inside the vehicle.

questions.explanation: A person attending a parked placarded vehicle must be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it with a clear view. They cannot be in the sleeper berth.

questions.question: What does Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table list?
questions.explanation: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table lists the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating for a placarded vehicle's power unit?
questions.explanation: Placarded vehicles must have a fire extinguisher with a UL rating of 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, where can you leave your vehicle unattended?
questions.explanation: You can only leave a vehicle carrying explosives unattended in a safe haven, which is an approved location for parking vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: What must a driver do at a railroad crossing when driving a vehicle with empty hazmat cargo tanks?
questions.explanation: Drivers must stop at railroad crossings when their vehicle has cargo tanks used for hazardous materials, whether the tanks are full or empty.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating for placarded vehicles?
questions.explanation: Placarded vehicles must have a fire extinguisher with a UL rating of 10 B:C or higher.
